I will keep my full 10.1 mu in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the system I know best, it fits my land and irrigation, and at my age I want a steady and familiar plan instead of trying something risky. For wheat, I will use improved seed rather than old traditional seed, because I need stable emergence, disease resistance, and dependable yield. I will keep fertilizer at a moderate level, not too high, because my land is not large and I do not want to waste money. I will irrigate wheat a few key times with my well, because in Hebei wheat responds well to timely water. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage on a small farm than deep ploughing. For maize after wheat harvest, I will plant the full area again with hybrid seed, because hybrid maize gives me better yield and stronger performance. I will also keep maize fertilizer and irrigation at moderate levels and spray only when needed, because I want to control cost and labor while still protecting yield. My goal this year is stable production from both crops, manageable field work, and no unnecessary risk.
